rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief, intermittent happiness of morning contrasts with the much longer sorrows of life, as in 90:4.
rows.anchor: periods of happiness in human life, as contrasted with the much greater length of "the night when it grows still and dark"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As morning follows night, divine mercy will relieve every suffering in this life or the next; God has willed grace and mercy for Himself.
rows.anchor: as sure as morning follows night, God's mercy is bound to lighten every suffering, either in this world or in the life to come

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted thought is that only the thoughtless would infer rejection from the suffering God has willed the Prophet to bear.
rows.anchor: as the thoughtless might conclude in view of the suffering that He has willed thee to bear

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ash-Sharh was revealed almost immediately after Ad-Duha and appears to continue it directly.
rows.anchor: revealed almost immediately af ter the preceding one, appears to be a direct continuation of the latter

rows.speaker: Ta'us ibn Kaysan and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
rows.claim: They regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah and recited them in prayer without a second basmala; Asad cites Razi.
rows.anchor: Ta'us ibn Kaysan, or the Caliph Umar i bn Abd al-Aziz (known as "the Second Umar") - regarded Ad-Duha and Ash-Sharh as one surah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah addresses the Prophet first and, through him, every true follower of the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: addressed in the first instance to the Prophet and, through him, to every true follower of the Qur'an

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed after surah 85, The Great Constellations.
rows.anchor: REVEALED after surah 85 ("The Great Constellations")

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It states a fundamental moral truth shared by all true religious teachings.
rows.anchor: formulates a fundamental moral verity, stressing the fact that it is common to all true religious teachings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's title keyword comes from the mention of the fig in its first verse.
rows.anchor: key-word by which it is known - is derived from the mention of the fig

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best conformation means physical and mental qualities suited to the functions this creature is meant to perform.
rows.anchor: endowed with all the positive qualities, physical as well as mental, corresponding to the functions which this particular creature is meant to perform

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This relates to the Qur'anic idea that all creation, including the human self, is formed for its intended purpose.
rows.anchor: everything which God creates, including the human being or self (nafs), is "formed in accordance with what it is meant to be"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It does not mean equal bodily or mental endowments: each person can best use their own inborn qualities and environment, whatever their natural advantages or disadvantages.
rows.anchor: of his inborn qualities and of the environment to which he is exposed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fall results from humans corrupting their original positive disposition through their own actions and omissions.
rows.anchor: consequence of man's betrayal - in another word, corruption - of his original, positive disposition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad directs readers to his note on 2:7 for the attribution of this reduction to God's action.
rows.anchor: Regarding the attribution, by God, of this "reduction" to His Own doing, see note 7 on 2:7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an early Meccan surah, probably revealed after At-Tin (surah 95).
rows.anchor: An early Meccan surah, most probably revealed after surah 95 (At-Tin)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden calamity is the Last Hour, which will bring a terrifying transformation of the world.
rows.anchor: the coming of the Last Hour, which will involve a terrifying transformation of the world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions of people and mountains are allegories for conditions understood through comparisons with physical phenomena within human experience.
rows.anchor: conditions which can be understood only by means of comparisons with physical phenomena lying within the range of human experience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This early Meccan surah is a powerful prophetic passage about humanity's unbounded greed.
rows.anchor: THIS early Meccan surah is one of the most powerful, prophetic passages of the Qur'an

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It especially addresses greed-driven tendencies that have come to dominate technological societies.
rows.anchor: the tendencies which have come to dominate all human societies in our technological age

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exclusive pursuit of these gains blocks spiritual insight and acceptance of limits grounded in moral values.
rows.anchor: A passionate pursuit of such endeavours, to the exclusion of everything else, bars man from all spiritual insight

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pursuit gradually destabilizes individuals and whole societies, eliminating their chance of happiness.
rows.anchor: with the result that not only individuals but whole societies gradually lose all inner stability and, thus, all chance of happiness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unrestrained economic growth destroys the natural environment and brings frustration, unhappiness, and confusion to people losing their remaining spiritual orientation.
rows.anchor: fundamentally wrong mode of life: an allusion to the gradual destruction of man's natural environment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unchecked pursuit of economic growth has brought frustration and confusion and threatens the remnants of spiritual and religious orientation.
rows.anchor: an overriding, unrestrained pursuit of "economic growth" is bound to bring - and has, indeed, brought in our time - upon a mankind that is about to lose the remnants of all spiritual religious orientation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takathur means greedily striving to increase benefits, whether tangible or intangible, real or illusory.
rows.anchor: The term takathur bears the connotation of "greedily striving for an increase", i.e., in benefits, be they tangible or intangible

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here it means obsessively seeking more comforts, material goods, and power over other people.
rows.anchor: In the above context it denotes man's obsessive striving for more and more comforts, more material goods, greater power over his fellow-men

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed shortly after surah 94, Ash-Sharh.
rows.anchor: REVEALED shortly after surah 94

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike dahr, which denotes unlimited time without beginning or end, asr signifies passing time that cannot be recovered.
rows.anchor: dahr, which signifies "unlimited time", without beginning or end: i.e., "time absolute"). Hence, asr bears the connotation of the passing or the flight of time - time which can never be recaptured

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asr denotes measurable time made up of a succession of periods.
rows.anchor: The term "asr denotes "time" that is measurable, consisting of a succession of periods

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
rows.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

rows.speaker: some commentators
rows.claim: Some commentators date verses 4–7 to Medina, but Asad rejects this view for lack of historical or textual evidence.
rows.anchor: The view of some commentators that verses 4-7 were revealed at Medina lacks all historical or textual evidence and may, therefore, be disregarded.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ma'un includes small daily-use items and occasional kindnesses that help others with such things.
rows.anchor: comprises the many small items needed for one's daily use, as well as the occasional acts of kindness consisting in helping out one's fellow-men with such items

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More broadly, al-ma'un means aid or assistance in any difficulty.
rows.anchor: In its wider sense, it denotes "aid" or "assistance" in any difficulty
